title: Consciousness does not emerge, it complexifies

statements.text: Hunt and Schooler adopt panpsychism, on a weight-of-plausibility judgment and preferably in Whitehead’s version, as the answer to the hard part of the hard problem. Consciousness is always present at some level, even in the simplest processes, and becomes more complex as matter does. Schooler is also open to consciousness emerging at some level of nested information processing.

sources.quote: This first step is particularly powerful if we adopt a Whiteheadian version of panpsychism
Consciousness is, rather, always present, at some level, even in the simplest of processes
